pairs.why: A is a wall clock seen straight on and lying flat against its wall, like the real card, while B's round clock stands on the floor on its bare rim with no stand and would roll.
B's key rows run parallel to the tilted body's edges and shrink with it, while A's key grid sits more front-facing on the tilted face and its keypad has no '=' key.
B is a four-wheeled wagon whose small front wheels hold the bed up consistently, while A's big near wheel is drawn almost face-on beside a box seen at an angle.
A's X-legged armchair has every part joined and standing on the floor, while B's front seat bar sticks out past the seat and its back frame floats behind the legs instead of connecting to them.
A's deck clearly rests on its posts, with the rope and life ring hung on them, while B's deck sits at uneven heights and its life ring hangs on a post standing in front of the deck.
B is a wall clock seen straight on and lying flat against its wall, while A's clock balances on its bare rim on the floor with no stand.
B's checkerboard rows stay parallel to the stone slab's edges, while A's board looks slightly rotated against the slab and has too many squares for a chessboard.
B's four-wheeled wagon holds its bed up consistently, while A's cart has its only axle at one end and leans on a shaft propped on the ground, so it is barely balanced.
